methodology: Multi-criteria weighted evaluation applying Ponytail minimalism principles

options_evaluated.name: Fully Native Android + iOS (Zero Shared KMP)
options_evaluated.description: Android written in Kotlin/Compose, iOS in Swift/SwiftUI. All math, geofencing, first-mile heuristics, and models implemented twice independently.
options_evaluated.ponytail_verdict: REJECTED. Duplicating spherical trigonometry (Haversine R=6371.0088km), first-mile walking threshold boundaries (800m/1500m), and consensus verification algorithms invites drift between iOS and Android. Violates deterministic parity contract.

options_evaluated.name: KMP Generated Contracts & API Models Only
options_evaluated.description: KMP project generates serialization DTOs and API contract data classes, but domain algorithms (first-mile, timetable solver) live in platform code.
options_evaluated.ponytail_verdict: REJECTED. Generates complex Swift mapping overhead for simple JSON DTOs while missing the actual valuable deterministic algorithmic parity.

options_evaluated.name: Small KMP Deterministic Domain Core + Fully Native UI (Selected)
options_evaluated.description: Pure Kotlin stdlib only. No UI, no network, no DB, no serialization, no coroutine runtimes in shared framework. Contains only: GeoPoint, HaversineDistance, OdishaBounds, FirstMileEngine, TimetableEngine, SearchFilterEngine, RideVerificationEngine, and Provenance Enums.
options_evaluated.ponytail_verdict: SELECTED. The laziest, cleanest solution that guarantees deterministic mathematical parity. 13 files, 0 third-party dependencies, standard library only. Compiles to static XCFramework for iOS and standard Gradle dependency for Android. Zero risk of KMP UI complexity.

options_evaluated.name: Large Shared KMP Application Core (Compose Multiplatform / Shared Architecture)
options_evaluated.description: KMP handles networking (Ktor), local persistence (SQLDelight/Room KMP), state machines (Decompose/Voyager), and/or Compose Multiplatform UI.
options_evaluated.ponytail_verdict: REJECTED. Gross over-engineering. High maintenance burden, fragile CocoaPods/SPM bridge, crippled SwiftUI idioms, bloated binary size, and severe Swift concurrency friction.

strictly_excluded_from_kmp: UI components or views (No Compose Multiplatform)
Networking layer (No Ktor in shared; native URLSession and Retrofit/OkHttp)
Local persistence (No SQLDelight; native SwiftData on iOS and Room on Android)
Location providers (No multiplatform location libraries; native CoreLocation and FusedLocationProviderClient)
Dependency injection frameworks (No Koin in shared)
formal_decision.ponytail_guardrail: Any proposed addition to mobile/shared must pass the 3-question test: 1) Is it pure deterministic domain logic? 2) Does it have zero external dependencies? 3) Does failure to share it create high risk of calculation drift between iOS and Android?
